Alex,

I'm happy to try, but once I got all of the extra packages installed I hit all kinds of parsing errors. NA Date values caused problems. Now non-NA datetime values are not parsing right. I seem to have fixed those, but there's no DEPTH in your sample dataset.

library(lubridate)
library(sp)
library(tidyverse)

data2 <- read_csv("~/Downloads/Sample_7G_data.csv") %>%
filter(!is.na <http://is.na>(LAT), !is.na <http://is.na>(DATE))

coordinates(data2) <- c("LON","LAT")
proj4string(data2) <- CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=NAD83")  ## for example...not sure which projection this was in?

data2utm <- spTransform(data2, CRS("+proj=utm +zone=10 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs"))

data2 <- as.tibble(data2utm) %>%
rename(Easting = LAT, Northing = LON) %>% #makes Lat and Lon = northing and easting
mutate(TIME = seconds_to_period(TIME) # make seconds into HMS
, TIME = sprintf('%02d:%02d:%02d', hour(TIME), minute(TIME), second(TIME)) # print it out as HH:MM:SS
, DATETIME = paste(DATE, TIME, sep=" ") # paste date and time together
, DATETIME = ymd_hms(DATETIME, tz="Etc/GMT-7"))  %>% # parse date into right time zone
distinct(TRANSMITTER, DATE, TIME, .keep_all = TRUE) # keep only unique TRANSxDATExTIME

Haven't had a chance to look at this in detail yet, but you should be able to plot these as points in a map following pretty much the same code from my blog. My blind guess is the parts you may need to tweak will be along these lines:
Making sure there are no NA's
The times are formatted as POSIXct (and potentially aggregated or rounded)
Adding a grouping to the aes() which is related to the times or the data...I'll need to look but ggplot and ggmap often need a grouping factor to plot spatial data.
Fortify the data so it's read for ggmap.
I'll try to take a look this weekend, otherwise come by the D-RUG meeting and we can figure it out.

Adios,
Ryan

Alex,

This is what I'm thinking, but there's a few caveats to this approach. I've allocated your transmitters as shape. Once you get past six transmitters, you really won't be able to differentiate them easily. You could facet them by transmitter or facet them in groups of transmitters, if that makes sense for your data. The color I've repurposed to represent time, but scaling color by date is a PITA so I had to hack the breaks. This was the color changes as time goes on. Your example data doesn't show this (at all).

You probably also want to show depth as well. We've used color and shape, so perhaps you could so size for depth, but that could lead to difficulty in interpretation.

B

library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(sp)
library(ggmap)

data2 <- read_csv("~/Downloads/Sample_7G_data (1).csv") %>%
filter(!is.na <http://is.na>(LAT), !is.na <http://is.na>(DATE)) %>%
mutate(LON2 = LON, LAT2 = LAT)

coordinates(data2) <- c("LON","LAT")
proj4string(data2) <- CRS("+proj=longlat +datum=NAD83")  ## for example...not sure which projection this was in?

data2utm <- spTransform(data2, CRS("+proj=utm +zone=10 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs"))

data3 <- as.tibble(data2utm) %>%
dplyr::rename(Easting = LAT, Northing = LON) %>% #makes Lat and Lon = northing and easting
dplyr::mutate(TIME = seconds_to_period(TIME) # make seconds into HMS

, TIME = sprintf('%02d:%02d:%02d', hour(TIME), minute(TIME), second(TIME)) # print it out as HH:MM:SS
, DATETIME = paste(DATE, TIME, sep=" ") # paste date and time together

, parsed = ymd_hms(DATETIME, tz="Etc/GMT-7")

)  %>% # parse date into right time zone

dplyr::mutate(DEPTH = if_else(DEPTH > 0, DEPTH*-1, NA_real_)) %>% #Change depth to negative values, anything negative already will be NA, 0 will stay same
dplyr::distinct(TRANSMITTER, DATE, TIME, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% # keep only unique TRANSxDATExTIME
dplyr::arrange(parsed)

tags <- as.data.frame(table(data3$TRANSMITTER)); tags     # provides a list showing number of detections by transmitter

###########Plotting Trajectories on map #######################
# Get the basemap
#look at data to get coordinates
map <- get_map(location = c(lon = -122.47, lat = 37.81), zoom = 13, crop = T, scale = "auto",
              color = "color", maptype = "satellite")  # can change to terrain
gg <- ggmap(map, extent = "panel", padding = 0)  # call the basemap

# Add points. Note plot will produce warnings for all points not in the
# lat/lon range of the base map layer.

#fortify data for plotting (make sure data is in POSIXct form, no NAs, and fortify data)

fortify(data3)

myBreaks <- function(x){
    breaks <- c(min(x),median(x),max(x))
    attr(breaks,"labels") <- as.POSIXct(breaks, tz = "Etc/GMT-7", origin = strptime("1970-01-01 00:00:00", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"))
    names(breaks) <- attr(breaks,"labels")
    return(breaks)
}

###Plot
gg + geom_point(data = data3, aes(x=LON2, y = LAT2, shape = TRANSMITTER, colour = as.numeric(parsed))) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low="lightblue", high="red", breaks=myBreaks) +
    labs(color="Date")

> This is what I'm thinking, but there's a few caveats to this approach. I've allocated your transmitters as shape. Once you get past six transmitters, you really won't be able to differentiate them easily. The color I've repurposed to represent time, but scaling color by date is a PITA so I had to hack the breaks. This was the color changes as time goes on. Your example data doesn't show this (at all).
>
> You probably also want to show depth as well. We've used color and shape, so perhaps you could so size for depth, but that could lead to difficulty in interpretation.

> , TIME = sprintf('%02d:%02d:%02d', hour(TIME), minute(TIME), second(TIME)) # print it out as HH:MM:SS

> )  %>% # parse date into right time zone

>

>

>
> #fortify data for plotting (make sure data is in POSIXct form, no NAs, and fortify data)

>
> myBreaks <- function(x){
>     breaks <- c(min(x),median(x),max(x))
>     attr(breaks,"labels") <- as.POSIXct(breaks, tz = "Etc/GMT-7", origin = strptime("1970-01-01 00:00:00", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"))
>     names(breaks) <- attr(breaks,"labels")
>     return(breaks)
> }
>

messages.body_plain:
Hey R Users,

Do you know if it is possible to run an anova between dataframes? I am trying to see if I can combine two replicate experiments, and each experiment has several different measurements in different units (percentages, distance/time, etc). I know how to compare data for a single column of data, but is it possible to compare all the data at once?

Here is an example script, pasted below as text and also attached as an r script.

I know how to run an anova such as (Measurement1~Sample.Name*Experiment.Number) etc. But is it possible to combine all the data so I can compare all measurements in one comparison?

My ultimate goal is to test if the samples (Sample.Name) and the experiment (Experiment.Number) have a significant interaction or not.

Many thanks!

-----

#Creating a Dataset
Sample.Name<-paste("Sample",1:100,sep="")
Sample.Code<-replicate(100, paste(sample(LETTERS, 3, replace=TRUE), collapse=""))
Time.Point<-c(replicate(50, paste(1)),replicate(50, paste(2)))
Measure1<-runif(100)
Measure2<-runif(100,min=0,max=0.5)
Measure3<-c(runif(50,min=0,max=30),runif(50,min=15,max=100))
Experiment1<-data.frame(Sample.Name,Sample.Code,Time.Point,Measure1,Measure2,Measure3)
Experiment2<-data.frame(Sample.Name,Sample.Code,Time.Point,Measure1,Measure2,Measure3)
#Is it possible to run an anova between both dataframes, to see if they can be combined?
#Combining both experiment's data into a new dataframe "combined.data"
Experiment1$Experiment.Number<-1
Experiment2$Experiment.Number<-2
combined.data<-rbind(Experiment1,Experiment2)
#Is there a way to run an anova across all the data, looking for a difference in the variable "Experiment.Number"?
#If I try concatenating the response variables I get an error message
summary(aov(lm(c(combined.data$Measure1,combined.data$Measure2,combined.data$Measure3)~combined.data$Sample.Name*combined.data$Experiment.Number)))
#For now I am only able to compare each measurement individually, as shown below
summary(aov(lm(combined.data$Measure1~combined.data$Sample.Name*combined.data$Experiment.Number)))
summary(aov(lm(combined.data$Measure2~combined.data$Sample.Name*combined.data$Experiment.Number)))
summary(aov(lm(combined.data$Measure3~combined.data$Sample.Name*combined.data$Experiment.Number)))

Hi there,

If you have multiple response variables, you have entered the realm of multivariate statistics. Instead of ANOVA (analysis of variance) you need to be running a MANOVA (multivariate analysis of variance).

However, your error is caused by something more basic. Instead of using "c" to bind your response variables, use "cbind". For example:

manova(cbind(Measure1, Measure2, Measure3)~ Experiment.Number, data = combined.data)

This worked fine for me.

Since we are on the topic of multivariate analysis, I would recommend looking into the "adonis" function from the "vegan" package instead of the manova function that comes with base R. It is a permutational MANOVA technique that is a little more robust.

require(vegan)
adonis(cbind(Measure1, Measure2, Measure3)~ Experiment.Number, data = combined.data)

Hope that helps,
Rosie

> Hey R Users,
>
> Do you know if it is possible to run an anova between dataframes? I am trying to see if I can combine two replicate experiments, and each experiment has several different measurements in different units (percentages, distance/time, etc). I know how to compare data for a single column of data, but is it possible to compare all the data at once?
>
> Here is an example script, pasted below as text and also attached as an r script.
>
> I know how to run an anova such as (Measurement1~Sample.Name*Experiment.Number) etc. But is it possible to combine all the data so I can compare all measurements in one comparison?
>
> My ultimate goal is to test if the samples (Sample.Name) and the experiment (Experiment.Number) have a significant interaction or not.
>
> Many thanks!
>
> -----
>
> #Creating a Dataset
> Sample.Name<-paste("Sample",1:100,sep="")
> Sample.Code<-replicate(100, paste(sample(LETTERS, 3, replace=TRUE), collapse=""))
> Time.Point<-c(replicate(50, paste(1)),replicate(50, paste(2)))
> Measure1<-runif(100)
> Measure2<-runif(100,min=0,max=0.5)
> Measure3<-c(runif(50,min=0,max=30),runif(50,min=15,max=100))
> Experiment1<-data.frame(Sample.Name,Sample.Code,Time.Point,Measure1,Measure2,Measure3)
> Experiment2<-data.frame(Sample.Name,Sample.Code,Time.Point,Measure1,Measure2,Measure3)
> #Is it possible to run an anova between both dataframes, to see if they can be combined?
> #Combining both experiment's data into a new dataframe "combined.data"
> Experiment1$Experiment.Number<-1
> Experiment2$Experiment.Number<-2
> combined.data<-rbind(Experiment1,Experiment2)
> #Is there a way to run an anova across all the data, looking for a difference in the variable "Experiment.Number"?
> #If I try concatenating the response variables I get an error message
> summary(aov(lm(c(combined.data$Measure1,combined.data$Measure2,combined.data$Measure3)~combined.data$Sample.Name*combined.data$Experiment.Number)))
> #For now I am only able to compare each measurement individually, as shown below
> summary(aov(lm(combined.data$Measure1~combined.data$Sample.Name*combined.data$Experiment.Number)))
> summary(aov(lm(combined.data$Measure2~combined.data$Sample.Name*combined.data$Experiment.Number)))
> summary(aov(lm(combined.data$Measure3~combined.data$Sample.Name*combined.data$Experiment.Number)))
